title: gate_spans reads any name ending in run_gate as a gate call: no word boundary on its match
body:
gate_spans (tests/lib/test_helper.bash), the one reader the gate scans share (dispatch.bats 0087's split-argv arm and runlog.bats 0085's --source arm), starts a span on any non-comment line holding `run_gate ` followed by a space, as a substring with no word boundary. So a name that merely ends in run_gate reads as a gate call: WP02c's local `unrun_gate` did, at three lines of lib/cmd/release's pre-flight, and both scans reported "a run_gate with no bare --" there until the variable was renamed unrun_entry. Earlier the same day the hook-in's `declare -F run_gate` dependency check in lib/release.macos read as a call too (fixed by dropping the check, which seal_verdict already covers).

A name is the wrong fix each time it happens. The reader should match run_gate as a word: preceded by start of line, whitespace or a shell operator, and followed by a space, so `unrun_gate x` and `declare -F run_gate` are not spans while every real call still is. The arms' own non-vacuous checks (0087 counts the split sites a second way, 0085 refuses an empty span list) keep a narrowed reader honest.

Low: no wrong answer reaches a user; the cost is a false red in the whole suite, met only there. For after the release (vc, 2026-11-01).

## Resolution

Fixed at 6845d6d202cc5e032df9338e272d4c7072b4f941, landed on main by devbin-vc's land-stack.sh from the tested tip f59f4d68, whose paths it equals, unpushed until the 0.1.20 cut. gate_spans now opens a call only where a command starts: at the start of a line after any indentation, after a shell operator (`;`, `&`, `|`, `(`, `{`, `!`), or after a keyword that starts a command (`if`, `then`, `do`, `else`, `elif`, `while`, `until`, `time`). Whitespace before the name is not enough, since `declare -F run_gate` has it, so a name that ends in run_gate and run_gate as an argument open no span. Over lib/ and bin/ the old reader and the new give the same ten spans. dispatch.bats's contract arm for the reader gains a call after indentation, one after an operator and one after a keyword, which are rows, and `unrun_gate` and `declare -F run_gate`, which are not. It was proved on its own test, under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 that each fix runs its own test alone, in light slot 01M6N09AVNVHARM1K7Z6FXHJVQ on devbin-vc's desk: the changed arm was red as wanted in red-0316 (6553e3d4), the base's code with the unit's dispatch.bats on top (want 8 rows, got 10, both NOTCALL lines opening spans), and at f59f4d68 under BSD dispatch.bats (128 of 128) and runlog.bats (133 of 133), the two files that call gate_spans, were green, each whole. The GNU legs, the tree scans, the critic and the whole suite run once, before the cut.
